title.text: workharbor: web UI and whr CLI mock, with example data

history.text: Chats grow large. Purge transcript removes messages, tool output and diffs; audit entries and a record of the purge stay. Clear view only hides older events.

phone.text: Phone: decisions first, chat and approvals on one screen. Installable PWA in release 1; the phone chat reaches the same live session.

cli.text: Every action in the web UI has a whr command. Exit code 6 means a task needs human input, 10 that it failed. whr usage reports tokens and cost; whr purge deletes transcript content and keeps the audit entries.

push.text: ntfy push: task ID, event kind and a link only. Never issue text or code, and no approve button. Approvals stay behind your login.

v0.text: In v0 the web UI is a remote for the agent: live chat, send, start, pause, resume, cancel, decisions and approvals. Pause is a hard interrupt; resume relaunches from the session. After v0: open in editor and takeover.

login.text: auth_expired and quota_exhausted are blocking Decisions. The run pauses, the task awaits guidance, the workspace and session are kept, and you log in again from the UI.

onboarding.text: First-run wizard: sign in, install the workharbor GitHub App and verify the ruleset, agents and default mode, host checks (untested items are marked), ntfy.

pushflow.text: Agents never push. Cleanup pins a commit SHA and opens a "Ready to push?" review; on approval the supervisor pushes as the workharbor GitHub App and opens the PR. The task stays ready for review until the PR is merged.

usage.text: Usage per run and task: tokens in, out and cache, and cost marked reported or estimated. With a subscription login the five-hour and seven-day windows lead and cost is notional.

approvals.text: Approvals have a deadline (10 minutes by default) and fail closed: expired or superseded counts as deny. Input is capped at 2,000 characters and marked as truncated; a review approval names its commit SHA.
